children: TMK Energy
reports that the 2026 work program at its Gurvantes XXXV pilot well project in southern Mongolia’s South Gobi Basin is progressing to plan.
The LF-03 and LF-02 production wells have been re-completed with optimised well bores and smaller fit-for-purpose pumps now installed.
This follows an earlier pressure build-up test at LF-02 that confirmed further reservoir pressure decline in line with prior reservoir modelling.
Over the 14-day testing period, LF-02 produced 25.2 million standard cubic feet of gas with the pump switched off (hence no water production).
Increased Water Levels
Water levels were reported to have increased by approximately 170 metres, and the well required topping up with fluid before the pump could be pulled, yet gas continued to flow throughout.

Bottomhole pressure increased to 1,269 kilopascals at the top of the coal, and was stable over the final week of the test, which is interpreted to be at or very close to the desorption pressure at the LF-02 location.

When the well was restarted, gas production rose to 14.4Mscf per day—or close to three times the 5Mscf/d produced before recompletion—before easing back to pre-workover rates over the following day as the water column was drawn down.
The ultimate success of the re-completions will be determined over the coming months, after which TMK will decide if it will carry out the same operations on remaining wells LF-01, LF-04, and LF-07.
New Drilling Campaign
Drilling activities are scheduled to commence this week on new production well LF-08, the only additional pilot well in the 2026 program.
The rig arrived on location earlier this month, and is awaiting the availability of the contractor’s senior drilling crew, who have been engaged on another drilling project in Mongolia.
The well is scheduled for completion within two weeks following drilling and will be brought into production soon after.
The LF-02 well will be shut-in during the drilling of LF-08 to minimise any reservoir damage to either well.
Results from LF-08 are expected to guide TMK’s 2027 appraisal program, currently in the planning phase.
Advancing to Plan
TMK chief executive officer Dougal Ferguson said the Gurvantes XXXV work program commenced a few weeks ago and was advancing to plan.
“LF-03 and LF-02 have been re-completed with smaller casings and smaller fit-for- purpose pumps installed into the two wellbores,” he said.
“Both wells have successfully been restarted, which confirms that the re-completions are mechanically operating and able to produce water and gas to surface.”

“Drilling at LF-08 is due to commence this week—the rig is on location and the conductor has been set so when the crew arrives, they should be able to hit the ground running and completed the work within a couple of weeks.”
“We remain fully funded for this work program and are continuing towards our target of proving commerciality in 2026 ahead of an appraisal period next year.”

title: TMK Energy Advances Work Program at Gurvantes XXXV Pilot Well Project in Mongolia
